chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa or a man, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked:
About the woman who has been divorced three times, is there for her a dwelling and expenses?' He said: 'Is she pregnant?' I said, 'No'. He said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: Does a woman divorced three times receive housing and maintenance after the divorce?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that a woman divorced by a triple talaq (talaq al-thalathah) loses her right to both housing (sukna) and financial support (nafaqah), provided she is not pregnant. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the triple divorce constitutes a final, irrevocable separation (talaq ba'in), thereby terminating the ongoing marital obligations that typically persist until the end of the waiting period (iddah). The distinction regarding pregnancy highlights that the waiting period for a pregnant woman extends until childbirth, preserving her rights during that specific duration.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, or a man, from Hammad, from Shuayb, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having been asked about the woman divorced thrice, is there a dwelling for her and expenses?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is she pregnant?’ I said, ‘No’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa or a man from Hammad from Shu’ayb from abu Basir who has said the following: “Once abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked

about the case of a woman who is divorced three times; if she deserves maintenance and accommodation. He (the Imam) asked, ‘Is she pregnant?’ I replied, ‘No, she is not pregnant.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘No, she does not deserve it.’”
